title: Mamaliga
subtitle: Romanian polenta with cheese and cream
excerpt: Coarse cornmeal is cooked slowly in milk and water until thick, then served with crumbled feta and soured cream. Mamaliga is Romania's staple food, eaten at almost every meal in rural Romania for centuries. Simple, filling, and deeply satisfying.
sourceNotes: Mamaliga is Romania's staple food. Made from cornmeal, it is eaten at almost every meal in rural Romania. It predates potatoes in the region and was the food of peasants for centuries. Today it is celebrated as a national comfort food.

content.text: Mamaliga is the Romanian equivalent of polenta -- coarse cornmeal cooked low and slow until it pulls away from the sides of the pan. The key is pouring the cornmeal in a very thin, steady stream while whisking. Rush this step and you get lumps. Take it slowly and you get silk.

items.prepNote: use coarse cornmeal or polenta -- not wheat flour

content.text: Combine milk, 300ml cold water, and salt in a large saucepan. Bring to a gentle boil.
Reduce heat to low. Add the cornmeal in a very thin, steady stream, whisking constantly as you pour.
Switch to a wooden spoon and stir vigorously. Cook on the lowest heat for 20-25 minutes, stirring often, until the polenta is very thick and pulls away from the sides.
Stir in the butter. Serve in bowls or turn out onto a board. Top with crumbled feta and soured cream.

items.fix: Add in a very thin, steady stream and whisk constantly as you pour.

content.text: Romania, Moldova, and parts of Ukraine. Eaten as a side, a base, or a full meal. In traditional villages it was cooked in a cast-iron cauldron over an open fire and cut with a string rather than a knife.
